anomalies.observed: On the bottom M5Stack bus connector J2 the +5V global label is attached to pin 27 (pin 25 carries the spare net 'PIN25'), but on the top connector J1 the +5V label is attached to pin 25 and pin 27 is left unlabeled. The two supposedly identical pass-through connectors therefore map +5V to different header pins.
anomalies.expected: Spec §2/§4: 'identical nets on both so the board can be stacked between the M5Stack Core and a lower module (pass-through)' and 'The same +5V net is also tied directly to J1/J2 pin 27 (the M5Stack bus's 5V pin)'. Both J1 and J2 pin 27 must carry +5V.

evidence.quote: J1 (Conn_02x15_Odd_Even) left column bottom: ...PIN23, +5V (at the pin-25 row), BAT; pin 27 has no net label. J2 left column bottom: ...PIN23, PIN25, +5V (at the pin-27 row), BAT.
The same +5V net is also tied directly to J1/J2 pin 27 (the M5Stack bus's 5V pin)

anomalies.impact: The M5Stack Core supplies 5 V on bus pin 27, which is now unconnected on J1, so the board's +5V rail is not powered from the Core (only from the external 5 V input through D1). Meanwhile the Core's pin 25 is shorted to the board's +5V rail (and to the servo/PortB 5 V), which on the M5Stack bus is not the 5 V pin (likely GND/a spare), risking a 5 V-to-GND short through the Core and breaking the 5 V pass-through to any module stacked below J2.
